sources.title: UK Parliament, Government of the Raj 1858-1914
sources.note: Direct institutional account read. Government, nationalists and Indian electors sections. Restrictive early councils are not projected onto all later constitutional arrangements.

sources.title: National Army Museum, Independence and Partition, 1947
sources.note: Direct article read, Self-government, Partition, Law and order, Bloodbath and End of Empire sections. Avoid its disputed numerical death estimate and compressed June announcement date.

sources.title: The National Archives, Britain’s India policy, draft announcement of 20 February 1947 (FO 371/63529)
sources.note: Original archival transcript read through indexed source. Reproducible query: site.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/resources/indian-independence/britains-india-policy/ "paramountcy". Direct page fetch intermittently fails.

sources.title: National Army Museum, Third Burma War
sources.note: Direct indexed institutional article read. Origins, River campaign, Annexation and Guerrilla war. Secure years 1885 and 1886 used; no contested day from a different museum timeline.

sources.title: The Penguin, 3 April 1937, Secretary of State for Burma, Falkland Islands National Archives
sources.note: Original archival newspaper PDF indexed text read. Page headed Saturday 3 April 1937, page 2, Secretary of State for Burma: separation on 1 April and establishment of separate department. Not a modern webpage date.

sources.title: House of Commons Library, Jallianwala Bagh massacre (2019)
sources.note: Direct briefing read, introductory historical overview and paragraph noting disputed death toll. No single exact casualty count adopted.

sources.title: Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust, Background to the Salt Satyagraha
sources.note: Direct dated timeline read, 2, 5 and 12 March 1930 entries with Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi volume XLIII references.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, Indian textiles
sources.note: Direct museum essay read, textiles under industrial competition and swadeshi sections; object 0120(IS), Gujarat khadi about 1867. No modern craft demonstration projected into a particular historical household.

sources.title: M. K. Gandhi, Third Class in Indian Railways (1917), digitized by Project Gutenberg
sources.note: Original collection read, title essay printed pp.3-7, dated Ranchi 25 September 1917. Statements are explicitly Gandhi’s observations and reform proposals; his unsupported medical causation is not adopted.

sources.title: Drexel University College of Medicine Legacy Center, Anandibai Joshee
sources.note: Direct archival research guide read: biography, food and sari paragraphs, 1886 graduation and intended Kolhapur appointment, 1887 death; linked holdings include admissions correspondence and course records. No unqualified first Indian woman doctor claim.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Santiniketan
sources.note: Direct nomination summary and Outstanding Universal Value, Brief synthesis read. 1901 residential school, 1921 university and open-air classrooms under trees.

sources.title: C. V. Raman and K. S. Krishnan, A New Type of Secondary Radiation, Nature 121 (1928), 501-502
sources.note: Original publisher preview read, experiment paragraph and Calcutta affiliation. Publication 31 March 1928. No precise discovery day inferred from the letter’s dateline.

sources.title: M. K. Gandhi, Hind Swaraj, Gujarati digital edition, MKGandhi.org
sources.note: Direct 102-page PDF text read, title હિન્દ સ્વરાજ and preface dated 22-11-1909 on PDF page 7. This is a modern digital edition, not a claimed first-edition facsimile. Web screenshot failed, so access is text extraction rather than visual certification.

sources.title: Government of India Press Information Bureau, Gandhi Heritage Portal launch and key texts (2013)
sources.note: Original official account read through indexed text and reopened directly, The Key Texts section: 1909 manuscript, December Indian Opinion publication, 1910 translation titled Indian Home Rule and Bombay ban.

sources.title: National Army Museum, Medal awarded to Indian soldier demonstrates substantial role India played in First World War
sources.note: Direct museum account read. Cursetjee and the 14th Sikhs in Mesopotamia; 26-29 October 1918 fighting and quoted London Gazette citation dated 26 May 1919.

sources.title: Wallace Murray to Frank Cissel, 28 August 1943, Foreign Relations of the United States, volume IV, document 337
sources.note: Original diplomatic memorandum read directly in Office of the Historian edition. Paragraphs 1-5: starvation, hospital admission, proposed rice allocation and shortage of shipping. One contemporary report, not a complete causal model of the famine.

sources.title: Jawaharlal Nehru, The Demand to Quit India, 31 July 1942, Nehru Archive
sources.note: Original statement indexed text read and reopened directly: independence entails British withdrawal and proposed provisional government could represent Congress and Muslim League. Used as a political proposal, not proof that such a coalition was formed.
